text: Functions are reusable blocks of code that take inputs and return outputs.
Define a function with def, [laugh] give it a name and parameters in parentheses.
The return statement sends a value back to wherever the function was called.
Good functions do one clear job, which makes your code easier to read, test, and reuse later.
Call functions by name with arguments in parentheses.
Parameters can have a default value, making them optional — call without it and Python fills in the default.
[sigh] A function can return more than one value at once — Python packs them into a tuple automatically.
[chuckle] You can also write a short docstring in triple quotes right under def, describing what the function does.
And unpacking that tuple into two variables at once reads naturally — low, high equals min_max of the list.
[groan] One gotcha: a function with no explicit return statement quietly returns None.
